title: Graceful shutdown must stop accepting work, drain active requests and release/expire owned leases

original_titles.title: No graceful shutdown drain or lease release

problem: The worker/API process lifecycle does not implement a coordinated drain that stops claiming jobs, waits for active jobs/requests and releases leases safely before exit.
impact: During deployment or host restart, an active scoring/auto-submit job may be interrupted or unnecessarily held until lease expiry; shutdown behavior is not a controlled operational protocol.

evidence_paths: backend/worker.py: main loop and signal handling
verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Handle SIGTERM/SIGINT in API and worker. Mark the instance draining and stop accepting new mutations/job claims.
Wait a bounded grace period for active HTTP requests and jobs to finish. If a job cannot finish, release its lease only after confirming it is safe to retry.
Use idempotency for scoring and auto-submit jobs so a retry after interruption cannot duplicate side effects.
Expose shutdown/draining state in readiness and logs; add a test that terminates a worker mid-job and verifies safe requeue.

acceptance_criteria: No new jobs are claimed after drain begins.
In-flight work finishes or is safely requeued without duplicate awards.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
